text.p: Shares in chemical firm Solvay lost nearly three percent on Wednesday as investors continued to dump the share following last week's disappointing 1996 preliminary profits.
Solvay has lost almost six percent of its share value since February 6 when its 1996 preliminary results were announced.
Excluding 2.1 billion francs in exceptional gains, net profit fell by eight percent to 11.5 billion francs for 1996.
"Recent reports on the plastics prospects in Europe for 1997 show an uncertain outlook and this has affected Solvay," said one trader.
By 1500 GMT the share was down 1.86 percent at 21,050 francs, with over 300 million Belgian francs worth of Solvay shares traded.
Bank Degroof said Solvay's preliminary figures for 1996 were slightly below market consensus forecasts.

"After the share's marked outperformance of mid-January, we changed our recommendation from 'buy' to 'hold'. Even though Solvay's share price has recently come under pressure, we rate the share a hold," the bank said in a research note.
It added that the global capacity growth in plastics in 1998 could cause worries on margin erosion.
"Accordingly, we have become more cautious and see only limited potential for Solvay to outperform this year".
